_meta: Two RGBA pixels being averaged into one, as happens when an image with transparency is downscaled, blurred, or mipmapped -- every output pixel is a weighted average of input pixels. opaque_red is a fully opaque red pixel (alpha 1.0). transparent_blue is a FULLY TRANSPARENT pixel (alpha 0.0) that still carries a leftover color of blue in its RGB channels -- which is normal, because the color of a 0-alpha pixel is invisible and undefined, so authoring tools leave whatever was there. The trap: averaging the RGB channels and the alpha channel SEPARATELY (straight, non-premultiplied) lets the transparent pixel's invisible blue leak into the result, producing a purple fringe. The fix is to premultiply each pixel's color by its alpha BEFORE averaging (so a transparent pixel contributes zero color), average, then un-premultiply. background is a backdrop to composite the averaged result over, to show the fringe. The pixel colors and alphas are the fixture; every average and composite is computed.
